conviction_note: The findings sum to +0.85. The scaled number is +0.42 (p_up 53 x abs 7.0). Every positive here is a quarter or a booking that the company's own guide and its Oct 23 8-K already told the market about, and this name sold its last two beat-and-raise prints (-1.05%, -0.95%). The upside-paid skew (-7 vol pts) and 18.6% short interest lean up but give no sign the market is wrong. So p_up sits only just above 50, and abs_move_pct stays at the option-implied ~6.7-7%, not below it.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue of about $412-414M. Three estimate sources agree within 0.6%: Earnings Whispers $411.7M (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/TEM/21357, 2026-10-26), Chartmill $413.9M (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/TEM/estimates) and Benzinga $413.8M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TEM/earnings-forecasts). EPS: non-GAAP consensus -$0.07 to -$0.13 with a whisper of -$0.01. Q2 printed positive GAAP EPS against a -$0.15 consensus and the stock still fell, so EPS is not the line the stock trades on. The company guide is FY2026 revenue $1.595-1.605B with adj. EBITDA ~$65M (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260730328545/en/Tempus-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results). That implies H2 revenue of $864-874M against H1's $730.6M, so the bar sits inside the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest: 18.57% of float, 3.55 days to cover (MarketBeat snapshot 2026-10-30, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/tempus-ai-nasdaqtem-stock-price-down-74-should-you-sell-2026-08-24/). A FINRA-based figure shows 25.1M shares short and 3.2 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement, per a search snippet. The 25-delta skew is -7.03 vol pts (calls bid over puts), put/call OI is 0.44, the event-implied move is 6.72% and the 7-day straddle 12.16%, all from the baseline. The stock ran from ~$49 at the Q2 print to an ~$89-90 high, sat at $77.84 on 10-29, and fell ~8% intraday on 10-30 to ~$71.7. The only 10-30 headline found is a 10b5-1 CEO sale. Short interest is fairly crowded and the options market leans up.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-07-30) management said core oncology volume growth accelerated to 31%, June was one of the strongest months to date, MRD volume reached ~9,000 (+38% q/q), hereditary growth should reach mid-teens by year-end, and data bookings were ~$200M with Insights +36%. That supports Q3 revenue at or slightly above the ~$412-414M consensus (+23% y/y vs Q2's +22%). Q3 sits inside the FY guide, which requires H2 of $864-874M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats with a raised FY guide drew -1.05% (2026-05-05) and -0.95% (2026-07-30). The Q4 2025 print, where guidance underwhelmed, drew -7.32% (2026-02-24). Beats are typically sold on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the consensus already sits at guide-consistent ~+23%. Only the momentum detail (June strength, the volume acceleration, the MRD ramp) argues for a modest beat over that. If the market had priced a bigger beat, the consensus would sit above the guide-implied run-rate, and it does not.
findings.independence: Q2 release on BusinessWire (same company, same quarter): https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260730328545/en/Tempus-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results. Peer NeoGenomics' NGS volume +17% in Q3 is a separate finding below.

findings.finding: Earnings Whispers (2026-10-26) puts FY2026 revenue consensus at ~$1.59B, just below the low end of the $1.595-1.605B guide. If that holds, a reiterated guide is itself a small beat against FY consensus and a raise (Tempus has raised every quarter in 2026) a larger one. TIKR says the FY consensus matches the guide, so the gap is disputed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY revenue guide raised at Q1 and Q2 2026, with reactions of -1.05% and -0.95%. A raise has not paid on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: If the Street fully underwrote the guide, FY consensus would sit at or above $1.595B. One source says it does not, and a second says it does, so the gap is real but small and contested.
findings.independence: Contradicting source: TIKR says '2026 consensus matches company guidance of about $1.6 billion', https://www.tikr.com/blog/tempus-ai-gains-6-as-bristol-myers-squibb-licenses-oncology-data. Capped small because the two sources disagree.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-23 Tempus disclosed in an 8-K multi-year agreements worth $192.5M over about five years: a $137.5M BMS oncology data/Lens SOW through 2031 and a $55M Pathos neuro data order. That is roughly $38M a year of incremental data revenue against a Data & Applications run-rate of ~$373M a year. These are Q4 bookings that support the FY/Q4 guide and the data-growth narrative on the call; they do not change Q3 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose ~6% on 2026-10-23 and ~8.4% on 2026-10-27, mostly giving it back by 10-30. On the print day, data bookings (~$200M in Q2) came with a -0.95% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock already reacted. What remains is that management can now cite Q4-to-date bookings and possibly firm the H2 guide on the call. A full pricing would show in consensus Q4 data revenue, and that change is not visible yet.
findings.independence: Value figures confirmed by a German report citing company disclosure: https://trading-treff.de/aktien/tempus-ai-aktie-eu-zertifizierung-fuer-xr-tumortest (2026-10-27). Deal described in the TIKR article (2026-10-23). All three rest on the same disclosure.

findings.finding: Peer NeoGenomics reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-28, after Tempus last spoke. It showed NGS revenue +29%, NGS test volume +17% and revenue per clinical test +11%, and raised its FY revenue and EBITDA guide, while total clinical volume grew only ~2%. Oncology NGS demand held up in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of TEM reacting to peer prints. TEM's own oncology volume growth (+31% in Q2) runs well ahead of NEO's.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy only. NEO is a heme- and pathology-heavy lab with a different mix, and its +2% total clinical volume cuts the other way. TEM's reaction to NEO's print can't be separated from the 10-28/10-30 swings.
findings.independence: Proxy for the industry, not confirmed by Tempus. Guardant (Nov 5) and Caris report after the window.

findings.finding: CMS's preliminary CY2027 Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule (2026-09-21) aligns Medicare lab rates with private-payer rates, about $1B a year in savings with cuts capped at 15% a year through 2029, final in November. Any 2027 commentary on the call could carry a reimbursement headwind for the Diagnostics book outside the ADLT-priced tests. ADLTs are not mentioned.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline turned on CLFS. Tempus usually gives next-year color at JPM in January (2026-01-12 bmo +4.51%), not on the Q3 call.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission: Tempus has not quantified any exposure, and its main tissue tests migrate to ADLT pricing, with a ~$200 ASP uplift from 2027 per management. If the market saw a material hit, lab peers would have de-rated in late September. Nothing found shows that.
findings.independence: None. Proxy, not confirmed by the company.

findings.finding: The Personalis merger proxy/prospectus (424B3 dated 2026-10-21) discloses Tempus management's June 2026 projections for Personalis as a Tempus subsidiary: revenue $79M/$115M/$172M and adj. EBITDA -$95M/-$86M/-$73M for 2026/2027/2028. That is a drag larger than Tempus's entire 2026 adj. EBITDA guide (~$65M), and Tempus may pay up to 50% in cash, debt-funded. Any 2027 framing that includes Personalis would show a lower EBITDA path than standalone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal announcement on 2026-07-20 preceded the Q2 print (-0.95%). Management said on the Q2 call that EBITDA and FCF improve in 2027 'even with Personalis'.
findings.why_not_priced: These numbers sit deep in a 540k-character proxy, in the 'Unaudited Prospective Financial Information - Tempus' section, and no preview found quotes them. The Earnings Whispers preview only frames Personalis as a 'financing and timing' question. If the market had absorbed a ~$86M 2027 EBITDA drag, 2027 EBITDA estimates and the 'durable profitability' framing would show it. On the money side, it buys an MRD platform that Tempus says is ramping (9k tests in Q2), so this is a near-term earnings question and not distress.
findings.independence: The Q2 call (MarketBeat transcript) says Tempus will debt-fund much of the cash portion and that 2027 EBITDA improves anyway, which partly offsets this. Different document, opposite lean.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: the stock rose ~46% after Q2 to an ~$89-90 high, then fell back. It closed $77.84 on 10-29 and dropped ~8% intraday on 10-30 to ~$71.7 with no company news beyond a 10b5-1 CEO sale. Short interest is 18.57% of float (3.55 days), the 25-delta skew is -7 vol pts (calls bid) and put/call OI is 0.44, all leaning up into a bmo print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The bmo prints in the baseline were both up (+4.51% 2026-01-12, +3.63% 2025-08-08). The amc prints went down 5 of 6.
findings.why_not_priced: The pre-print de-risking on 10-30 lowered the entry and the run-in. A crowded short against a beat-and-hold is a squeeze mechanism. But the skew already shows upside paid for, so most of this is in the option price.
findings.independence: Short interest from the MarketBeat snapshot (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/tempus-ai-nasdaqtem-stock-price-down-74-should-you-sell-2026-08-24/); skew and P/C from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: CEO Eric Lefkofsky sold 250,000 shares on 2026-10-27 at $67.36-72.31 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-03-08 (Form 4 filed 10-29), after similar plan sales on 9-17 and 9-22. He keeps ~8.5M via Gray Media, ~14.7M via Blue Media and ~10M in GRATs plus direct holdings.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on the print line. The sale headline ran on the morning of 10-30, the day of the ~8% drop.
findings.why_not_priced: Scheduled plan sales carry no information about the quarter, and the headline is already in the 10-30 price. Filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: Personalis shareholder vote on the Tempus merger is set for 2026-11-30 (record date 10-15). HSR expired 2026-10-02. Tempus's cash/stock election comes later, and the stock floor of $48.42 is far below spot.
Final CY2027 CLFS rates from CMS are due in November 2026, probably after 11-02.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly up, in line with the upside-paid skew (-7 vol pts) and the crowded short. They cut against the name's habit of selling beat-and-raise prints and against a stock that has already doubled off the Q2 level.
lessons_applied: Lessons 1 and 6 (beats sold; the quarter lands inside the guide): Q2-momentum reported-quarter finding cut from +0.8 to +0.4, print_vs_bar from +1.0 to +0.8, p_up from 54 to 53
Lesson 6 (bar disputed): FY-consensus-below-guide finding capped from +0.3 to +0.2 because TIKR contradicts Earnings Whispers
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): NeoGenomics read-through cut from +0.3 to +0.2
Lesson 7 (negatives into 18.6% short interest and an upside skew): CLFS cut from -0.2 to -0.1, Personalis EBITDA drag from -0.4 to -0.3
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): Personalis cash/debt kept as an earnings-path question, not distress; it buys an MRD platform that is ramping
BMS/Pathos bookings cut from +0.4 to +0.3 as already reacted to; CEO 10b5-1 sale cut from -0.1 to -0.05 as routine
abs_move_pct left at 7.0, around the event-implied 6.72%, per the core's rule not to shrink it for sign uncertainty
